title: Applying logic operators and truth tables
footer: 2.4 Lesson 2: Applying logic operators and truth tables
starter: A microwave only runs when the door is shut and the start button is pressed. A car beeps if either front door is open. Which logic gate does each one behave like?
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: Setting out a truth table
facts: List every combination of inputs. Each input doubles the rows: 2 inputs give 4 rows, 3 give 8, 4 give 16.
Then work out the output for each row.
stations.challenge: How many rows would a truth table with 5 inputs need?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: List every combination of inputs. Each input doubles the rows: 2 inputs give 4 rows, 3 give 8, 4 give 16.
Also credit: Count up in binary: 00, 01, 10, 11.

questions.q: How many rows does a truth table with 3 inputs need?
How many rows does a truth table with 4 inputs need?

stations.name: Electric circuits
facts: Two switches in a row (series): the bulb lights only if both are on. That's AND.
Two switches side by side (parallel): the bulb lights if either is on. That's OR.
stations.challenge: Design a circuit with switches that behaves like an OR gate.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Two switches in a row (series): the bulb lights only if both are on. That's AND.
Also credit: Two switches side by side (parallel): the bulb lights if either is on. That's OR.

questions.q: Two switches in series control a bulb. Which gate does this represent?
Two switches in parallel control a bulb. Which gate does this represent?

stations.name: NOT AND, NOT OR
facts: NOT (A AND B): work out A AND B, then reverse every result.
NOT (A OR B): work out A OR B, then reverse every result.
An intermediate column for the bracket makes this easier.
stations.challenge: Complete both truth tables at this station.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: NOT (A AND B): work out A AND B, then reverse every result.
Also credit: NOT (A OR B): work out A OR B, then reverse every result.

questions.q: Complete the truth table for Q = NOT (A AND B).
questions.a: Truth table for Q = NOT (A AND B) over 2 inputs (4 rows); output is 1 wherever the expression is true

questions.q: Complete the truth table for Q = NOT (A OR B).
questions.a: Truth table for Q = NOT (A OR B) over 2 inputs (4 rows); output is 1 wherever the expression is true

stations.name: Three inputs
facts: With three inputs there are 8 rows.
Use intermediate columns for each gate.
(A AND B) AND NOT C: work out A AND B, then NOT C, then AND them together.
stations.challenge: Which rows of (A AND B) AND NOT C output 1?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: With three inputs there are 8 rows.
Also credit: Use intermediate columns for each gate.

questions.q: Complete the truth table for Q = (A AND B) AND NOT C.
questions.a: Truth table for Q = (A AND B) AND NOT C over 3 inputs (8 rows); output is 1 wherever the expression is true

stations.name: NOT A AND (B OR C)
facts: Work out NOT A in one column and B OR C in another.
Then AND those two columns together.
The output is 1 only when A is 0 and at least one of B and C is 1.
stations.challenge: Explain why every row where A = 1 gives an output of 0.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Work out NOT A in one column and B OR C in another.
Also credit: Then AND those two columns together.

questions.q: Complete the truth table for Q = NOT A AND (B OR C).
questions.a: Truth table for Q = NOT A AND (B OR C) over 3 inputs (8 rows); output is 1 wherever the expression is true

stations.name: Four inputs
facts: Group the inputs: (A OR B) and (C AND D) can be worked out separately.
Then combine the two intermediate columns.
stations.challenge: Write the expression for the diagram in the experience.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Four inputs need 16 rows.
Also credit: Group the inputs: (A OR B) and (C AND D) can be worked out separately.

questions.q: For Q = (A OR B) AND (C AND D), which must be true for Q to be 1?
questions.a: C and D must both be 1, and at least one of A and B must be 1

questions.q: Write the Boolean expression for this logic diagram.
questions.a: Q = (A AND B) OR (C AND D) (or any equivalent expression)

final.name: Final challenge: detective's table

questions.q: Complete the truth table for Q = (A OR B) OR NOT C.
questions.a: Truth table for Q = (A OR B) OR NOT C over 3 inputs (8 rows); output is 1 wherever the expression is true

final.note: Students should have predicted these on the worksheet before tapping the star. Mark the prediction, not just the final answer.

exam.q: State how many rows a truth table needs for four inputs.
points: List every combination of inputs. Each input doubles the rows: 2 inputs give 4 rows, 3 give 8, 4 give 16.
With three inputs there are 8 rows.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark for a correct answer.

exam.q: Complete a truth table for Q = NOT P OR (Q AND R) on the back of this sheet.
points: List every combination of inputs. Each input doubles the rows: 2 inputs give 4 rows, 3 give 8, 4 give 16.
Then work out the output for each row.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 8.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
Repeating the question in the answer and stopping there.
